newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian oil-producing communities want royalties.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian oil-producing communities want royalties.

text.p: Oil-producing communities in Nigeria have recommended the military government directly allocate a percentage of royalties on crude oil production to them, the national news agency reported on Sunday.

It quoted a statement issued on Saturday at the end of a three-day seminar on relations between oil companies and their host communities as saying this measure would make the communities feel they have a stake in crude oil production.
Executives of oil multinationals, leaders of oil-producing communities, and state oil company officials attended the seminar in the capital Abuja.
Oil-producing communities often complain that the oil activities of the multinationals are damaging the environment and have been seeking compensation in return.
"The royalties percentage could be withheld as sanctions for acts of vandalism against properties of oil companies," the communique said.
Oil companies sometimes accuse the oil-producing communities of deliberately causing spillages by vandalising their pipelines and machines.
The communique called for ongoing dialogue between the oil companies and their host communities to eliminate "suspicion and mutual distrust."
Crude oil is the economic backbone of Nigeria, accounting for slightly more than 90 percent of its foreign exchange earnings.
